passages.title: The Picnic Nobody Will Forget
passages.passage: Last month my cousins and I decided to have a picnic (1)____ the lake near my grandmother's village. We had planned everything carefully, or (2)____ we thought. My aunt packed sandwiches, fruit and a big bottle of lemonade, and my brother was (3)____ charge of the blanket and the games. The morning was bright and warm, so we set (4)____ early, laughing and singing on the way. The trouble started as soon as we arrived. First, we discovered that the blanket was still lying on the kitchen table at home. Then, (5)____ we were spreading our jackets on the grass instead, a group of ducks marched over and began to eat our bread. My little cousin tried to chase them away, (6)____ he slipped on the wet bank and fell into the water up to his knees. By midday, dark clouds had gathered, and within minutes it was raining (7)____ hard that we could barely see the path. We ran back to the village, carrying (8)____ was left of the food, and arrived soaked and shivering. My grandmother laughed when she saw us, but she made us hot soup and lent us dry clothes. Looking back, that terrible picnic is probably the day we talk about (9)____ often when the family gets together. Next summer we are going to try again, and this time I (10)____ definitely check the bag twice before we leave.

questions.q: Blank (1): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: A picnic takes place beside (next to) a lake. Inside the lake is impossible, and among and between need more than one thing.

questions.q: Blank (2): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The fixed expression or so we thought means 'that is what we believed, wrongly'. As, such and too do not form this phrase.

questions.q: Blank (3): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: To be responsible for something is to be in charge of it. No other preposition is used with charge in this meaning.

questions.q: Blank (4): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Set off means to start a journey. Set up means to arrange or establish something, and set on or set down do not describe leaving.

questions.q: Blank (5): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: While introduces a clause with a subject and verb (while we were spreading). During is followed by a noun, not a clause; until and unless give the wrong meaning.

questions.q: Blank (6): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: He tried to chase the ducks, but he slipped: the second half is an unexpected contrast, not a result (so) or a reason (because). Although would need the clauses the other way round.

questions.q: Blank (7): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Before an adverb and a that-clause we use so ... that. Such goes with a noun, and too and very cannot be followed by that.

questions.q: Blank (8): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: What means 'the thing(s) that' and can begin a clause with no noun before it. Which and that need a noun to refer back to, and whom is for people.

questions.q: Blank (9): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The picnic is compared with all the other days the family remembers, so the superlative most often is needed. More often compares only two things, and much and many do not go before often.

questions.q: Blank (10): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Next summer and are going to place the sentence in the real future, so a promise takes will. Would belongs to an imagined situation, and might and could clash with definitely.

passages.title: Nobody Knew My Name
passages.topic: the first day at a new school
passages.passage: When my family moved to Da Nang in August, I was worried about starting at a new school (1)____ I knew nobody. On the first morning I woke up two hours (2)____ my alarm rang, put on my new uniform and stared at myself in the mirror. My mother, (3)____ had also changed schools as a child, told me that everybody feels nervous at first and that the feeling would pass. The school was (4)____ bigger than my old one, with three buildings and a large playing field. I got lost twice before I found my classroom, and by the time I sat down the lesson had already started. The teacher asked me to introduce (5)____, and I spoke so quietly that she had to ask me to repeat my name. At break, I stood alone (6)____ the corridor, pretending to read the notices on the wall. Then a girl with short hair walked up and asked (7)____ I wanted to join her table at lunch. Her name was Mai, and it turned (8)____ that she lived only two streets away from our new flat. We talked about music and discovered we liked the same bands. By the end of the day I had been (9)____ to a football team, a book club and a group chat with half the class. My mother was right, of course. (10)____ the time Friday came, I could not remember why I had been so afraid.

questions.q: Blank (1): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The clause describes the place in which the writer knew nobody, so the relative adverb where is needed. Which or that would need to be the subject or object of the clause, and when refers to time.

questions.q: Blank (2): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: A nervous person wakes up early, so two hours before the alarm. After would mean oversleeping, and until and since cannot follow two hours here.

questions.q: Blank (3): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The relative pronoun is the subject of had also changed and refers to a person, so it must be who. Whom is an object form, which is for things and whose shows possession.

questions.q: Blank (4): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: A comparative is strengthened with much (much bigger). Very and so go with the plain adjective, and more bigger doubles the comparative.

questions.q: Blank (5): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The subject and the object are the same person, so the reflexive pronoun myself is required. Me is a plain object, mine is possessive and my needs a noun after it.

questions.q: Blank (6): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: A corridor is an enclosed space, so we stand in it. On is for surfaces, at is for points, and by would mean next to it.

questions.q: Blank (7): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: A reported yes/no question begins with whether (or if). That reports a statement, while what and why report wh-questions.

questions.q: Blank (8): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: It turned out that means 'it was discovered that'. Turn up means to arrive, and turn on and turn over have unrelated meanings.

questions.q: Blank (9): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: People are invited to a team or a club. Asked would need to join, joined does not take to, and offered goes with the thing given, not with to a team.

questions.q: Blank (10): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The fixed phrase is by the time something happens. At, in and until are never used before the time + clause in this way.

passages.title: The Brown Wallet
passages.passage: Last Saturday I went into town to buy a present (1)____ my father's birthday. I spent an hour in the bookshop, chose a book about mountains, and reached into my pocket to pay. My wallet was gone. I searched every pocket twice and then emptied my bag onto the counter, but there was no sign (2)____ it. The shop assistant was kind and suggested I check the café where I (3)____ been sitting earlier. I ran back, but the table had already been cleared and nobody had handed anything in. My heart sank. The wallet had not only my money in it (4)____ also my student card and a photo of my grandmother. I sat on a bench outside the station, wondering how I was going to tell my parents. Just as I was about to give (5)____, my phone rang. An unknown voice asked whether I was the owner of a brown wallet. A cleaner at the café had found it under a chair and had used my student card to get (6)____ touch with the school, (7)____ then passed on my number. I walked back to the café as fast as I (8)____. The cleaner, an elderly man named Mr Tan, refused to accept any reward. 'Somebody did the same for me once,' he said. I bought the book for my father that afternoon, but I also bought a small cake for Mr Tan. Since then I have (9)____ left home without checking that my wallet is safely zipped inside my bag. It is a lesson I would rather have learnt (10)____ an easier way.

questions.q: Blank (1): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: A present is bought for an occasion or a person. To would follow give, not buy a present, and of and at do not fit.

questions.q: Blank (2): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The collocation is no sign of something. For, about and from are not used after sign in this sense.

questions.q: Blank (3): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Sitting in the café happened before the past moment of the story, so the past perfect continuous had been sitting is needed. Have is present, and was or would cannot be followed by been sitting with this meaning.

questions.q: Blank (4): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Not only is always paired with but also. And, or and so break the pair.

questions.q: Blank (5): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Give up means to stop trying. Give in means to surrender to someone, give out means to distribute, and give away means to donate.

questions.q: Blank (6): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: To contact someone is to get in touch with them. The phrase never takes on, at or into.

questions.q: Blank (7): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The clause adds extra information about the school, an organisation, so after the comma we use which. Who is for people, that cannot follow a comma in this kind of clause, and what is not a relative pronoun.

questions.q: Blank (8): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The story is in the past, so as fast as I could. Can is present, and was or did do not complete the comparison naturally.

questions.q: Blank (9): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The writer now always checks, so since that day he has never left without checking. Ever needs a negative or a question, always left without checking says the opposite, and yet goes at the end of a negative sentence.

questions.q: Blank (10): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: We do something in a certain way. By is used before a method noun without way (by post), and on and at do not go with way here.

passages.title: Twenty Minutes in the Chair
passages.passage: For weeks I had been (1)____ off a visit to the dentist. A tooth at the back of my mouth hurt every time I drank something cold, but I kept telling myself it would get better (2)____ its own. Of course, it did not. One evening the pain became so bad that I could not sleep, and my mother booked me an appointment (3)____ nine o'clock the next morning. I sat in the waiting room with a magazine I was not really reading, listening to the drill in the next room and feeling (4)____ nervous than I had ever felt before an exam. When my name was called, my legs felt like jelly. The dentist, Dr Huong, was a cheerful woman (5)____ voice was surprisingly calm. She looked at the tooth, took an X-ray and explained that there was a small hole which needed to be filled. 'It will be over (6)____ twenty minutes,' she promised. She gave me an injection so that I would not feel (7)____, and then she got to work. To my surprise, the worst part was the sound, not the pain. I stared at a poster on the ceiling and counted the letters (8)____ it to pass the time. When she finished, she showed me how to brush the back teeth properly and told me to (9)____ down on sweets and fizzy drinks. I walked out into the sunshine feeling foolish for having worried so much. If I had gone earlier, the hole (10)____ have been even smaller. Next time, I will not wait for the pain to tell me.

questions.q: Blank (1): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: To delay something is to put it off. Call off means to cancel completely, take off is what a plane does, and set off means to leave on a journey.

questions.q: Blank (2): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Without help is on its own. The similar phrase with by is by itself, so by its own is wrong, and in and at do not form the expression.

questions.q: Blank (3): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Clock times take at (at nine o'clock). On is for days, in for months and parts of the day, and by would mean 'no later than'.

questions.q: Blank (4): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The word than later in the sentence shows a comparison, so more nervous is needed. Most is the superlative, and much or very cannot be followed by than.

questions.q: Blank (5): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The voice belongs to the woman, so the possessive relative whose is needed before the noun voice. Who, which and that cannot show possession.

questions.q: Blank (6): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: In twenty minutes means twenty minutes from now. For gives a length of time something lasts, and during and since do not fit a future point.

questions.q: Blank (7): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: After not we use anything; not ... nothing is a double negative. Something belongs in positive sentences, and not feel everything changes the meaning.

questions.q: Blank (8): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Words printed on a poster are on it, because the poster is a surface. In is for containers, at is for points, and of shows possession.

questions.q: Blank (9): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: To eat less of something is to cut down on it. Put down, turn down and bring down exist, but none of them takes on with this meaning.

questions.q: Blank (10): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: If I had gone is a third conditional about the past, so the result needs would have been. Will belongs to the first conditional, and had or has cannot come before have been.

passages.title: Six Weeks at the Beach Café
passages.passage: The summer I turned sixteen, I decided that I wanted to earn some money of my (1)____ instead of asking my parents for it every week. My uncle owns a small café near the beach, and he agreed to let me work there (2)____ six weeks. On my first day I arrived at seven o'clock, full of confidence, and by nine I had already dropped a tray of glasses and given two customers the wrong change. My uncle did not shout. He simply handed me a broom and told me that everybody makes mistakes (3)____ first. After that, things slowly got better. I learned how to carry three plates at once, how to remember an order (4)____ writing it down, and how to smile at a customer who had been waiting far too long. The hardest part was not the work itself (5)____ the heat; by the middle of the afternoon the kitchen felt like an oven. At the end of each week my uncle paid me in cash, and I put most of it (6)____ a jar under my bed. I had promised (7)____ that I would save enough for a second-hand guitar. Some of my friends spent the summer sleeping late and playing games, and there (8)____ days when I envied them. But when September came, I had the guitar, a tan, and a pair of arms that were stronger (9)____ they had ever been. I also had something harder to describe: the feeling of having done something useful. If I (10)____ offered the job again next year, I will not hesitate.

questions.q: Blank (1): type one word.
questions.explanation: Of my own means belonging to me and nobody else. A word like pocket cannot follow of my; it would need my pocket money, with the noun after it.

questions.q: Blank (2): type one word.
questions.explanation: A length of time (six weeks) takes for. During is tempting but is used before the name of a period (during the summer), not before a number of weeks.

questions.q: Blank (3): type one word.
questions.explanation: At first means in the beginning. In first and on first do not exist; first alone would not need a preposition, but the blank must be filled.

questions.q: Blank (4): type one word.
questions.explanation: The skill is remembering an order and NOT writing it, so without + -ing is needed. Before writing it down would mean he still writes it, which is not the point being made.

questions.q: Blank (5): type one word.
questions.explanation: Not X but Y corrects one idea with another. And would make the sentence say both things were hardest, which contradicts not the work itself.

questions.q: Blank (6): type one word.
questions.explanation: Money is put into (or in, inside) a jar, because the jar is a container. On or at would place the money on the outside of the jar.

questions.q: Blank (7): type one word.
questions.explanation: The writer made the promise to the same person who made it, so the reflexive myself is required. Me cannot be the object when the subject is I.

questions.q: Blank (8): type one word.
questions.explanation: There + verb agrees with the noun after it, and days is plural and the story is in the past, so were. Was fails the agreement and are fails the tense.

questions.q: Blank (9): type one word.
questions.explanation: A comparative (stronger) is completed with than. As pairs with as strong, not with the -er form.

questions.q: Blank (10): type one word.
questions.explanation: Next year and I will not hesitate make this a first conditional, so the if-clause takes a present passive: am offered (informally get offered). Were offered belongs to the second conditional and clashes with will.
